# Reduce the macOS pytest cell to a platform-compatibility subset

## Context / Problem
The Gerrit Verified Gate's critical path is the macOS pytest cell. It runs the FULL default
suite plus the integration tier, while every other gate job finishes by ~20 min. Measured over
four recent successful runs the macOS py3.13 cell is ~2140-2486s and is the sole long pole
(gate ~43 min). On the IDENTICAL test selection the macOS runner is ~3.7x slower per test than
Ubuntu (macOS ~2140s vs Ubuntu ~572-595s), attributable to per-test process-spawn + git-store
fixture overhead — the CPU-bound AST/policy scanners are equal/faster on macOS. Running full
breadth on the slow runner buys latency, not confidence.

## Approach
Keep the full suite on Linux (Ubuntu 3.11/3.12/3.13 unchanged) and reduce the macOS cell to the
tests whose behaviour genuinely differs between Darwin and Linux: file locking (flock/fcntl/
mkdir), atomic directory/rename, subprocess timeout (gtimeout vs timeout), and cross-process git
contention. macOS keeps its existing `integration` tier step (cross-process concurrency
end-to-end) and runs a new `platform_compat`-marked subset in place of the full default suite.
Selection is centralised in ONE auditable place — a path-keyed auto-marker in tests/conftest.py
— rather than per-file markers, so the macOS suite cannot silently drift. This fits the goal of
cutting CI runtime without cutting confidence: Linux still runs everything.

## Scope
- pyproject.toml — register a `platform_compat` marker in the `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`
  `markers` list (the block currently ends at the `e2e:` entry).
- tests/conftest.py — extend the existing `pytest_collection_modifyitems` hook (which already
  auto-applies the `external` marker by path) to also apply `platform_compat` by path, driven by
  a documented `_PLATFORM_COMPAT_PATH_FRAGMENTS` tuple (store/lock/atomic/timeout/snapshot/
  contention seams).
- .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml — change the `DEFAULT_SUITE_MARKS` env expression
  (currently the two-branch ternary at the "Run the default suite" step) so the macOS cell
  selects `platform_compat and not external`; Ubuntu keeps its existing selection. The macOS
  integration-tier step is unchanged.
- tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py — update
  `test_repo_policy_nodes_run_only_in_the_existing_primary_cell` (its regex hardcodes the old
  two-branch `DEFAULT_SUITE_MARKS`) for the new three-branch expression, and add a guard that
  the macOS subset still collects the core OS-sensitive files.

## Testing
- Collect and run `-m "platform_compat and not external"` locally; confirm it selects the
  store-lock / timeout / snapshot / contention tests and passes.
- Run tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py (the CI-shape guard) to green.
- A new guard test asserts a representative set of platform-sensitive files (store lock,
  stamped_lock, timeout_budget, repo_snapshot, event_append_index_lock, atomic_ticket_dir_create)
  collect under the marker, so pattern drift fails loudly rather than silently emptying the macOS
  suite (the failure path).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A `platform_compat` marker is registered in pyproject.toml and `pytest -m platform_compat`
      collects a non-empty set. Evidence: marker registered; `pytest -m "platform_compat and not
      external and not integration" --co` collected 900 tests (16501 deselected).
- [x] tests/conftest.py auto-applies `platform_compat` by path via
      `_PLATFORM_COMPAT_PATH_FRAGMENTS`, and the macOS `DEFAULT_SUITE_MARKS` branch in
      _build-and-test.yml is `platform_compat and not external`. Evidence:
      test_repo_policy_nodes_run_only_in_the_existing_primary_cell passes against the
      three-branch expression (part of the 28-passing parity guard run).
- [x] The Ubuntu default-suite selection is unchanged — the primary/non-primary branches still
      read `not integration and not external` and `... and not repo_policy`. Evidence: same
      parity guard test asserts the Ubuntu branches verbatim; 28 passed.
- [x] tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py passes in full. Evidence: `pytest
      tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py -p no:xdist -q` -> 28 passed.
- [x] The platform_compat subset runs green locally via
      `pytest -m "platform_compat and not external and not integration"`. Evidence: 900-test
      subset collected and passed locally; the change also merged with Verified +1 on Gerrit
      change 2228 (full gate green).
